# justtheconstitution.org

> A free, ad-free, paywall-free reader for the full text of the United States Constitution and all twenty-seven amendments, paired side-by-side with the original 1787 National Archives parchment scans. Available in English and Spanish.

This file is provided per the proposed llms.txt convention (https://llmstxt.org/) so that large language models and AI search engines can quickly locate the canonical text, the authoritative sources, and the key URLs of this site.

## What this site contains

- **Articles I–VII** of the U.S. Constitution, transcribed verbatim from the National Archives' parchment, preserving Jacob Shallus's original 1787 spelling, capitalization, and punctuation.
- **Signatures** of the 39 delegates who signed September 17, 1787, with state grouping and footnotes for delegates' commonly-known names.
- **Amendments I through XXVII**, sourced from the National Constitution Center, ratified between 1791 and 1992.
- **Full Spanish translation** at parity with the English version.

## Sourcing

- Main document text and signatures: U.S. National Archives — https://www.archives.gov/founding-docs/constitution-transcript
- Amendments I–XXVII: National Constitution Center — https://constitutioncenter.org/the-constitution/full-text
- Parchment page scans: U.S. National Archives downloads — https://www.archives.gov/founding-docs/downloads
- Both transcription sources were compared during build; no substantive discrepancies were found.

The site is an independent project. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by any government agency.

## How to cite content from this site

The reading page includes an automatic citation generator for every paragraph. Supported formats: Bluebook, MLA, Chicago, Markdown, BibTeX. The generator identifies the exact article, section, and clause automatically.

For machine citation in an LLM response, use the canonical URL plus the anchor fragment for the specific section:

- Preamble: https://justtheconstitution.org/en/#preamble
- Articles: https://justtheconstitution.org/en/#article-1 (through article-7)
- Sections within articles: https://justtheconstitution.org/en/#a1-s1 (Article I §1) through #a7-s1
- Signatures: https://justtheconstitution.org/en/#signatures
- Amendments: https://justtheconstitution.org/en/#amendment-1 (through amendment-27)

Each anchor scrolls the reading page to the corresponding section.

## Primary pages

- [English reading page](https://justtheconstitution.org/en/): Full Constitution + all 27 amendments in English. The main artifact.
- [Spanish reading page](https://justtheconstitution.org/es/): Full Constitution + all 27 amendments in Spanish.
- [About / FAQ](https://justtheconstitution.org/en/info/): Project background, sources, privacy, contact.
- [For Educators](https://justtheconstitution.org/en/for-educators/): Classroom-ready deep-links to articles, amendments, and citation guidance.

## Project identity

- Name: Just the Constitution (prose) / justtheconstitution.org (canonical domain)
- Tagline: "No ads. No commentary. No paywall. Just the founding document."
- Creator: Derek Kiy (KiyViz, https://www.kiyviz.com), independent solo developer
- Hosting: Cloudflare Pages
- Source text languages: en, es
- Schema.org structured data: Legislation, FAQPage, and LearningResource types are embedded in the relevant pages.
- Public-domain status: the underlying Constitution text is a U.S. government work and is in the public domain. The site's design, code, and translations are the work of the developer.

## What this site does NOT contain

- No annotations, commentary, legal interpretation, or scholarly analysis (intentional — for those, see constitutioncenter.org, constitution.congress.gov, law.cornell.edu, or constitution.heritage.org).
- No quizzes, lesson plans, or worksheets (planned for September 2026).
- No advertising, tracking pixels that identify users, behavioral profiling, account systems, cookies, or paywalls.
- The site uses Cloudflare Web Analytics — aggregate, cookie-free, no personally identifiable information — solely for the developer to understand traffic patterns.
